title: Arriving in Chicago, finding Ellen Winston, peeling potatoes
summary: She walks into the Burlington Building, is sheltered by Miss Love until Ellen Winston arrives, and gets a job peeling potatoes at a Hyde Park boarding house.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And when I got to the building -- you know, like when you get off the streetcar, well, I was facing the building. So I walked upstairs in this building. There was a lady washing. Her name was Miss Love. So I said, "Lady, do you know a girl around here by the name of Ellen Winston?" She said, "No, I don't, child. What you doing here, where are you from?" And I said, "Well, I'm looking for Ellen Winston." She said, "Well, I'm asking you where you're from." So I said, "I'm from Memphis." She said, "Memphis?" I said, "yes, ma'am." She said, "Well, there's a girl that lives here by the name of Helen Winston, and this is her Sunday off. She works out in Hyde Park, so this is her Sunday off." So I said, "Well, will you please, ma'am, let me stay here until she comes?" And she said yes.
So when the girl came it was Ellen Winston, my mother's friend's daughter. And she let me stay there.
So how'd you know where to go?
I didn't know where to go. It was just fate. Fate, the hand of God. That's the reason I just have so much faith in God, Chris. It was just the hand of God that led me to this place, you see.

And so when the girl came, she said, "Pig, what in the world are you doing here?" And I said, "I didn't know where you lived, but I knew you were in Chicago." So she said, "Well, just sit down and take your coat off." I had
kept my coat on all the time, you know, waiting for her, even though the lady told me I was welcome. to come

So she said, "I'll take you out where I work." She was second cook up at this place, Hyde Park, you know. So she took me out there where she worked. But she put her dress on me and combed my hair down a little different. And I forget the lady's name -- I wish I could think of her name, she was such a nice lady, at own this Bodin House. So she told her that I was there from Memphis, and could she possibly find a way to give me some kind of little job to do. And the lady gave me the job peeling potatoes. So I peeled the potatoes. Got along well. I stayed there, too. Stayed there until the lady closed the boarding house. And when the lady closed the boarding house -- in the meantime, while I was there, you know what little time I went to school I used to sing at school, and they told me I could sing, you know.
